subject: Dedicated reservation: cluster floor + decoupled ramp architecture for HelixPath
messages:
From: Ben Caldwell <ben.caldwell@helixpath.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-28T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Capacity ask — dedication + burst questions

Irene / Karthik —

Thanks for the demo last week. The exec team liked Redwood's latency profile and the observability features. We're trying to map out a dedicated reservation that protects our production latency while giving us some burst headroom during model retraining and evaluation spikes. A few specific asks so we can move to procurement:

- What minimum cluster footprint do you recommend for our steady-state inference (we're currently at ~60 rps p50, 1.4 tokens/req average)?
- Can we decouple a reserved "floor" from burst capacity so we don't overcommit?
- What are typical ramp windows (weeks/months) you see for customers of our size?

If you can share a short options sheet with cluster sizes, min GPUs, and sample ramp schedules (fast, medium, conservative), that would be perfect.

Also attaching our current traffic sample for the last 30 days.

Thanks,
Ben Caldwell
Head of Platform, HelixPath
[Attachment: helixpath_30d_traffic_sample.csv (CSV, 128KB)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-11-28T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask — dedication + burst questions

Ben —

Appreciate the detail and the traffic sample. I've pulled together two deliverables attached: a short offer summary (helixpath_dedicated_offer_v2.pdf) and an editable sizing workbook (cluster_sizing_workbook.xlsx). High level upfront:

- Recommended steady-state floor: 20 GPUs (A100-equivalent) — this keeps 99th pct latency under your SLOs for the reported p50/p95 traffic mix and factors in 1.4 tokens/req average.
- Burst strategy: we can offer an uncoupled burst pool that sits outside the reserved floor and is billed on usage; you get guaranteed throughput from the floor while bursting into the pool for retraining/eval windows.
- Ramp windows: we propose three standard tracks — fast (4 weeks to full), medium (8–12 weeks), conservative (3-months plus staged validation). The workbook has explicit week-by-week activation triggers.

Quick asks from our side to finalize pricing: approximate committed term (12/24 months), expected monthly peak burst hours, and whether you need on-prem connectors for evaluation jobs.

Next steps: Karthik will add a technical appendix for model warmup, KV-cache sharing, and pre-warm policies — that will include recommended kernel/quantization profiles for lower unit cost. Jordan will follow up on contracting and DocuSign.

Irene

Subject: Re: Capacity ask — capacity math and ramp patterns

Ben / Irene —

Adding the technical sizing notes from the workbook — please see inline summary and the small table at the bottom for quick copy/paste into your infra spec.

Summary recommendations (derived from your 30-day sample):
- Steady floor: 20 GPUs (A100-eq)
  - Rationale: steady 60 rps p50 with 1.4 tokens/req; 20 GPUs gives ~70% utilization headroom for steady inference and allows KV cache reuse across workers.
- Min-GPU (activation safe point): 8 GPUs
  - We recommend a minimum live-set of 8 GPUs for high-availability in low-traffic hours; this prevents cold-cache latency degradation.
- Burst pool: 40 GPU-hours burst pool available per month (elastic), billed at on-demand uplift pricing; can be auto-provisioned for scheduled evaluation windows.

Ramp options (week granularity):
- Fast: Week 0 - provision 50% of floor (10 GPUs), Week 1 - 75% (15 GPUs), Week 2 - 100% (20 GPUs) + burst pool live. Ideal if you have QA automation and model tests ready.
- Medium: Week 0 - 25%, Week 2 - 50%, Week 4 - 75%, Week 8 - 100% (smoother validation).
- Conservative: Staged onboarding per product team; activate per-service canaries and add 2–4 GPUs per week until target.

Operational notes:
- Warmup: use a read-only warmup job that primes KV cache for heavy models (we can run the job first 48 hours at no extra charge during onboarding).
- Failover: if floor utilization exceeds 85% for >15 minutes we automatically route eligible requests to the burst pool or a lower-capacity compatible model variant (configurable).
- Cost controls: we can cap burst-spend per month and send alerts at thresholds.

Attachment: cluster_sizing_workbook.xlsx has the per-model token cost and a simulation tab. Happy to run a quick simulation if you share a 1-week sample of peak windows (UTC times).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
